title: Simplicity Object Format (SOF) object, JSON version 0
description: A compiled Simplicity contract whose parameters are not filled in yet: a body f : P -> 1 plus the schemas of its parameters and witnesses. Draft; see IR.md. Some rules can't be expressed in JSON Schema and are listed under $comment.
$comment: Also required, but not checkable here: body_cmr is the CMR of the decoded body; every type is in canonical text form (no non-canonical spelling such as 2^128*2^128); parameter names are unique; every key in signatures names a witness, and every key.param names a parameter; source_language is present if any source_type is; witnesses list one entry per witness node of the body, in non-sharing post order; sources lists the entry file first, then the files it imports sorted by path.

jet_set.description: Jet set of the body, identified by the hash of its canonical jet table.

body.description: The body f : P -> 1 in Simplicity's bit encoding without witness data, in base64 (RFC 4648 standard alphabet, padded), as Simplicity tools print programs.

source_language.description: The language the source_type fields are written in, such as simplicityhl. Required if any parameter or witness has a source_type.

params.description: The parameters. Their order defines P, the right-nested product p0 * (p1 * (... * p(n-1))), or 1 when there are none.

witnesses.description: One entry per witness node of the body, in the order a linker fills them (non-sharing post order). A witness used twice in the source can appear twice.

signatures.description: Witnesses that a PSBT/PSET signer fills, keyed by witness name. Each named witness has type 2^512 (Signature).

provenance.description: Where the object comes from, so that a third party can rebuild it and compare. Linkers ignore it.

type_text.description: A Simplicity type in canonical text form: 1, 2, 2^N, A+B, A*B and parentheses (section 5.3.1).

source_type.description: The type as the source language writes it, aliases included (Pubkey, Height, Either<Signature, Signature>), for people and tools that speak that language. Linkers ignore it.

name.description: The source-level parameter name, ASCII. Used directly as a descriptor key.

scheme.description: Signature scheme. Only bip340 is defined.

key.description: The parameter holding the public key. Omitted when the program takes the key from a constant or a witness.

param.description: Name of an entry in params.

message_builder.description: How the signed message is computed. An object with exactly one tag. Only the jet tag is defined, and only sig_all_hash. A signer that does not recognise the tag or the jet must not sign.

jet.description: Name of a jet of type 1 -> 2^256.

compiler.description: The compiler that produced the object, e.g. simc.

compiler_version.description: The exact compiler version. Different versions can produce different bodies.

entry_point.description: The function compiled as the body, for compilers that have a choice.

options.description: The compiler options that affect the output, in order, as passed to the compiler.

repository.description: Where to fetch the sources. A hint only: the sha256 of each source is what a verifier checks.

sources.description: The source files: the entry file first, then the files it imports, sorted by path.

url.description: URL of the repository, with a scheme such as https://. Not scp-style SSH shorthand (git@host:path), which can't be fetched without credentials.

commit.description: The commit holding the sources (SHA-1 or SHA-256 object name).

modified.description: True if a source file differed from that commit at build time.

path.description: Relative path with / separators: from the repository root when a repository is given, otherwise as given to the compiler (entry file) or from the entry file's directory (imports).

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the file's bytes, as sha256sum prints it.
